RIGHT OF REPRESENTATION, PER STIRPES, AND PER CAPITA AT EACH GENERATION (PROB. CODE §§ 240, 245-246) — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Alex Lee · September 9, 2026

PURPOSE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's statutory default rules for dividing property among a class of descendants when a member of the class has died leaving descendants of their own -- the rules the Probate Code uses for property taken "by right of representation," "per stirpes," or "per capita at each generation" (Probate Code §§ 240, 245, and 246). These sections can govern how a will, trust, or other instrument such as one Jordan Alex Lee signs is construed, and § 240's method is also cross-referenced by California's intestate succession statute when a decedent's issue are of unequal degree of kinship. This sheet states facts about California law generally. It does not determine how any specific will, trust, or other instrument's language will be construed, and it does not advise on what to do about a particular estate plan.

THE PER-CAPITA-AT-EACH-GENERATION DIVISION METHOD (§ 240)
When a statute directs that property be distributed "in the manner provided in" this section, a specific mechanical method applies: the property is divided into as many equal shares as there are living members of the nearest generation of issue then living, plus deceased members of that same generation who left issue then living. Each living member of that nearest generation receives one share, and the share that a deceased member of that generation would have received -- because that member left living issue -- is instead divided the same way among that deceased member's own then-living issue.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "If a statute calls for property to be distributed or taken in the manner provided in this section, the property shall be divided into as many equal shares as there are living members of the nearest generation of issue then living and deceased members of that generation who leave issue then living, each living member of the nearest generation of issue then living receiving one share and the share of each deceased member of that generation who leaves issue then living being divided in the same manner among his or her then living issue."
  — Cal. Probate Code § 240, Cal. Prob. Code § 240 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=240.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of an actual, codified mechanical division method -- not a claim about which state's law governs a specific instrument or estate, and not a claim about how any particular class gift's silence on method should be resolved. Section 240 states a single, undivided rule with no subdivisions to combine; no additional independent source was found for this.

DEFAULT RULE: A WILL OR TRUST THAT IS SILENT ON METHOD USES § 240 (§ 245)
Where a will, trust, or other instrument itself calls for property to be distributed "in the manner provided in Section 240 of the Probate Code," or where the instrument expresses no contrary intention and simply provides for issue or descendants to take without specifying the manner, the property is distributed using the § 240 method. Two kinds of wording, standing alone, are defined not to count as an expression of contrary intention that would displace this default: using "per capita" when the class's living members are not all of the same generation, and using contradictory wording such as "per capita and per stirpes" or "equally and by right of representation."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "(a) Where a will, trust, or other instrument calls for property to be distributed or taken “in the manner provided in Section 240 of the Probate Code,” or where a will, trust, or other instrument that expresses no contrary intention provides for issue or descendants to take without specifying the manner, the property to be distributed shall be distributed in the manner provided in Section 240. (b) Use of the following words without more, as applied to issue or descendants, is not an expression of contrary intention: (1) “Per capita” when living members of the designated class are not all of the same generation. (2) Contradictory wording, such as “per capita and per stirpes” or “equally and by right of representation.”"
  — Cal. Probate Code § 245, Cal. Prob. Code § 245 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=245.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of an actual default construction rule that fills a gap when a will, trust, or other instrument is silent, or uses certain specific wording, about how "issue" or "descendants" take -- not a claim about which state's law governs a specific instrument, and not a claim that any particular instrument's wording is or is not ambiguous or self-contradictory. This clause combines subdivision (a) with subdivision (b) and its two numbered examples, (b)(1)-(2), all part of the same statutory section; no additional independent source was found for this.

THE DIVISION FORMULA FOR A GIFT TO A DESIGNATED ANCESTOR'S CHILDREN (§ 246(A))
A related but distinct formula applies where a will, trust, or other instrument calls for property to be distributed "in the manner provided in Section 246 of the Probate Code": the property is divided into as many equal shares as there are living children of the designated ancestor, if any, plus deceased children who leave issue then living. Each living child of the designated ancestor is allocated one share, and the share of each deceased child who leaves living issue is divided the same way among that child's own issue -- a formula that starts counting from the designated ancestor's children specifically, rather than from the nearest living generation of issue as § 240 does.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "(a) Where a will, trust, or other instrument calls for property to be distributed or taken “in the manner provided in Section 246 of the Probate Code,” the property to be distributed shall be divided into as many equal shares as there are living children of the designated ancestor, if any, and deceased children who leave issue then living. Each living child of the designated ancestor is allocated one share, and the share of each deceased child who leaves issue then living is divided in the same manner."
  — Cal. Probate Code § 246(a), Cal. Prob. Code § 246(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=246.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of an actual, codified division formula keyed to a designated ancestor's children -- not a claim about which state's law governs a specific instrument, and not a claim about who qualifies as a "designated ancestor" or "child" in any particular instrument. This clause quotes subdivision (a) only; no additional independent source was found for this.

"PER STIRPES," "BY REPRESENTATION," OR "BY RIGHT OF REPRESENTATION" LANGUAGE (§ 246(B)-(C))
Using the words "per stirpes," "by representation," or "by right of representation" in an instrument triggers the § 246(a) formula, but the default's strength depends on when the instrument was executed. For an instrument executed on or after January 1, 1986, that wording calls for the § 246(a) method unless the will, trust, or other instrument expressly provides otherwise. For an instrument executed before January 1, 1986, the same wording also calls for the § 246(a) method, but only absent a contrary intent of the transferor -- a general contrary-intent inquiry, rather than the narrower express-provision requirement that applies to instruments executed on or after that date.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "(b) Unless the will, trust, or other instrument expressly provides otherwise, if an instrument executed on or after January 1, 1986, calls for property to be distributed or taken “per stirpes,” “by representation,” or “by right of representation,” the property shall be distributed in the manner provided in subdivision (a). (c) If a will, trust, or other instrument executed before January 1, 1986, calls for property to be distributed or taken “per stirpes,” “by representation,” or by “right of representation,” the property shall be distributed in the manner provided in subdivision (a), absent a contrary intent of the transferor."
  — Cal. Probate Code § 246(b)-(c), Cal. Prob. Code § 246(b)-(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=246.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of an actual default-construction rule for this specific wording, and of a genuine, dated distinction in how strong that default is depending on execution date -- not a claim about which state's law governs a specific instrument, and not a claim about what any particular transferor's contrary intent was or was not. This clause combines subdivisions (b) and (c), both part of the same statutory section; no additional independent source was found for this.

CERTIFICATION OF UNDERSTANDING
I certify that I have read this information sheet on California's statutory rules for distribution by right of representation, per stirpes, and per capita at each generation (Probate Code §§ 240, 245, and 246), and that this sheet states facts about the law generally rather than advising me on how any specific class-gift language in Jordan Alex Lee's will, trust, or other instrument will be construed or on what to do about my own estate plan.

Signed: _______________________ Date: September 9, 2026
At: Sacramento, California
